slides.h1: You Didn't Buy It Because It Was Good. You Bought It Because Everyone Was.
slides.sub: That's Rahu bias — the pull of the crowd, dressed up as research.

slides.body: This is a pattern-recognition tool for behaviour, not a promise about money or a stock pick. No placement or dasha guarantees a financial outcome.
Rahu (the north lunar node, the planet of craving) amplifies whatever is new, loud and rising. The result: FOMO buying, hype-chasing, and entering speculative bubbles late.

slides.h2: How it can show in the chart
points: Rahu in or aspecting the 2nd house (accumulated money)
Rahu linked to the 11th house (gains and the crowd)
Running a Rahu dasha or antardasha (period)
Context decides — none of these is a verdict on its own

slides.body: Rahu does not feel like impulse. It feels like finally spotting the thing everyone else has missed. The urgency itself is the signal to slow down.
Set a rule before the hype arrives: a cap on any single speculative position, and a 48-hour wait before acting on a tip. Let the rule, not the excitement, decide.
